Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 93, verses 1–5:

(p-6180)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Duha

Makki, and its verses are eleven.

A subtle point (latifah):

Ibn Kathir said: "We have related through the route of Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Bazza al-Muqri, who said: I recited to Ikrimah ibn Sulayman, and he informed me that he had recited to Isma'il ibn Qustantin and Shibl ibn Abbad. When I reached (wa'l-Duha), he said to me: 'Say the takbir until you complete it with the ending of every surah.' For we recited to Ibn Kathir and he commanded us with this. He also informed us that he had recited to Mujahid, and he commanded him with this, and Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, and he commanded him with this. Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and he commanded him with this, and Ubayy informed him that he had recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he commanded him with this."

This is a sunnah uniquely transmitted by Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Bazzi, from the descendants of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza. He was an imam in the readings (qira'at). As for hadith, Abu Hatim al-Razi weakened him and said: "I do not narrate from him." Likewise Abu Ja'far al-Uqayli said: "He is munkar al-hadith (his narrations are rejected)."

However, the Shaykh Shihab al-Din Abu Shamah related in (Sharh al-Shatibiyyah) from al-Shafi'i that he heard a man pronounce this takbir in prayer, and he said: "You have done well and you have followed the sunnah." This implies the soundness of this hadith. Then the reciters differed regarding the place of this takbir and its manner. Some of them said:

It is said from the end of ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ [al-Layl: 1]. Others said: from the end of ﴿By the morning brightness﴾. The manner of the takbir according to some of them is that one says "Allahu akbar" and stops, while among them are those who say "Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, wa'llahu akbar." The reciters mentioned, regarding the occasion of the takbir at the beginning of Surah al-Duha, that "when revelation was delayed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and paused for that period, then the angel came and revealed to him 'By the morning brightness and by the night when it is still' — the surah in its entirety — he said takbir out of joy and gladness." But this has not been related with a chain by which it may be judged sound or weak. And Allah knows best.

(p-6181)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[1–5] ﴿By the morning brightness﴾ ﴿and by the night when it is still﴾ ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the present life﴾ ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied﴾

﴿By the morning brightness (al-Duha)﴾: It has preceded in Surah ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾ [al-Shams: 1] the explanation of al-Duha as the light and the height of the day rising high.

﴿By the night when it is still (idha saja)﴾ [al-Duha: 2]: that is, its darkness has intensified. Its origin is from al-tasjiyah, which is covering, because it conceals with its darkness, as in the verse ﴿And We made the night a garment﴾ [al-Naba': 10].

﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you (ma wadda'aka)﴾ [al-Duha: 3]: this is the answer to the oath, meaning: He has not left you, nor cut you off in the manner of one who bids farewell.

Al-Shihab said in (al-Inayah): "So the tawdi' (farewell) is a metaphor, a continuative metaphor (isti'arah tab'iyyah), for leaving here, and in it there is a subtlety and magnification that is not hidden; for farewell only occurs between loved ones and those whose separation is grievous, as al-Mutanabbi said:

A remnant of a soul bade farewell the day they bade farewell, so I did not know which of the two departing ones to escort."

And he said in (Sharh al-Shifa'): "Wada' has two meanings in the language: leaving, and escorting the traveller. If it is interpreted here in the second sense by way of metaphor, there is in it an allusion that Allah has not left him at all, for He is with him wherever he is. Leaving would only be conceived on his side, and it is apparent. Along with its indication in this meaning of returning, for farewell is only for one who is loved and whose return is hoped for, and al-Urjani alluded to this in his saying:(p-6182)

When you see farewell, be patient, and let not distance trouble you;
and await the return soon, for the heart of farewell is that they return."

So His saying ﴿nor has He detested you﴾ [al-Duha: 3] confirms it. (He said): "I have not seen anyone mention this, despite its great subtlety, and they all interpreted it in the first sense." Since they saw that the form of the verb conveys increase in meaning and intensification, which entails complete severance, they said: the intensification is in the negation, not in the negated thing; so He left him for a judgment upon him, not because of harm from abandoning him, or for negating the condition and the conditioned. It was read: ﴿ma wadda'aka﴾ [al-Duha: 3] with lightened pronunciation (takhfif). And it occurs in a hadith: "The most evil of people is the one whom people leave out of fear of his obscenity." And it occurs in poetry, as in his saying:

"So what they sent forward for their own souls was greater in benefit than what they left behind."

For this reason, he said in (al-Misbah) concerning this: "Know that their saying in the science of morphology that the past tense of yada'u and yadharu is dead (amatu) is an error, and making it a metaphor from wadi'ah (deposit) is far-fetched." End.

Likewise he said in (al-Mustawfi): "All of it occurs in the speech of the Arabs, and the statements of the grammarians regarding it carry no weight; and when the river of Allah comes, the river of Ma'qil is nullified, even if it is rare." End.

And His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿nor has He detested you (qala)﴾ [al-Duha: 3]: that is, nor has He hated you. And al-qali is the one who hates. That is, He did not abandon you out of hatred.

Al-Shihab said: The omission of the object of "qala" is for brevity, since it is known, and so that it follows the pattern of the rhyme-endings (fawasil) after it, or lest He address him with what indicates hatred.

A note (tanbih):

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Abbas that "when the Qur'an was being revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ), Jibril was late to him for some days" (p-6183) so he was reproached for that; the polytheists said: "His Lord has forsaken him and detested him," so Allah revealed this verse. In another narration, the one who said that was the wife of Abu Lahab; in another, that it was Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her. There is no contradiction, given the possibility that it was uttered by all of them, except that the statement of the polytheists and the statement of Khadijah, if authentic, were an expression of grief and sorrow. In the narration of Isma'il, the mawla of the family of al-Zubayr, he said: "Revelation paused until it weighed heavily upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and saddened him. He said: 'I feared that my companion had detested me,' and then Jibril came with the surah 'By the morning brightness.'"

﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the present life﴾ [al-Duha: 4]: Ibn Jarir said: that is, and the abode of the Hereafter and what Allah has prepared for you therein is better for you than the worldly abode and what is in it. He says: so do not grieve over what has escaped you of it, for what is yours with Allah is better for you than it. Al-Qadi said: or: the end of your affair is better than its beginning, for he (ﷺ) continually ascends in elevation and perfection.

﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [al-Duha: 5]: that is, He will give you of the abundance of His blessings in the afterlife until you are satisfied. This is a generous and comprehensive promise, encompassing what Allah the Exalted gave him in this world of perfection of soul, knowledge of the first and the last, the manifestation of the matter and the elevation of the religion, through the conquests that occurred in his time (upon him be prayer and peace), and in the days of his rightly-guided successors and other Muslim rulers, and the spread of his call to the east and west of the earth, and what He stored up for him of honours that no one knows but Allah the Exalted. In sum, this verse comprises the aspects of honour, the kinds of happiness, and the scattered bounties of both abodes, in that He stated it in general terms and left it to His good pleasure, and this is the utmost of kindness and honour.

A note (tanbih):

In (al-Mawahib al-Ladunniyyah) he said: As for what the ignorant are deceived by, that he will not be satisfied with a single one of his community in the Fire, or that he will not be pleased for anyone of his community to enter the Fire, it is from the deception of Satan toward them and his playing with them; for he (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him) is pleased with what his Lord is pleased with, blessed and exalted is He, and He, glorified and exalted, enters into the Fire whoever deserves it from among the disbelievers and the disobedient. The Hashwiyyah have been zealous in strengthening such fabricated reports, deceiving the ignorant and adorning the paths of misguidance. There is no power and no strength except through Allah. And His saying, Exalted is He:

(p-6180)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Duha

Makki, and its verses are eleven.

A subtle point (latifah):

When I reached (wa'l-Duha), he said to me: 'Say the takbir until you complete it with the ending of every surah.' For we recited to Ibn Kathir and he commanded us with this. He also informed us that he had recited to Mujahid, and he commanded him with this, and Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, and he commanded him with this. Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and he commanded him with this, and Ubayy informed him that he had recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he commanded him with this."

This is a sunnah uniquely transmitted by Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Bazzi, from the descendants of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza. He was an imam in the readings (qira'at). As for hadith, Abu Hatim al-Razi weakened him and said: "I do not narrate from him." Likewise Abu Ja'far al-Uqayli said: "He is munkar al-hadith (his narrations are rejected)."

However, the Shaykh Shihab al-Din Abu Shamah related in (Sharh al-Shatibiyyah) from al-Shafi'i that he heard a man pronounce this takbir in prayer, and he said: "You have done well and you have followed the sunnah." This implies the soundness of this hadith. Then the reciters differed regarding the place of this takbir and its manner. Some of them said:

It is said from the end of ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ [al-Layl: 1]. Others said: from the end of ﴿By the morning brightness﴾. The manner of the takbir according to some of them is that one says "Allahu akbar" and stops, while among them are those who say "Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, wa'llahu akbar." The reciters mentioned, regarding the occasion of the takbir at the beginning of Surah al-Duha, that "when revelation was delayed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and paused for that period, then the angel came and revealed to him 'By the morning brightness and by the night when it is still' — the surah in its entirety — he said takbir out of joy and gladness." But this has not been related with a chain by which it may be judged sound or weak. And Allah knows best.

(p-6181)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[1–5] ﴿By the morning brightness﴾ ﴿and by the night when it is still﴾ ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the present life﴾ ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied﴾

﴿By the morning brightness (al-Duha)﴾: It has preceded in Surah ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾ [al-Shams: 1] the explanation of al-Duha as the light and the height of the day rising high.

﴿By the night when it is still (idha saja)﴾ [al-Duha: 2]: that is, its darkness has intensified. Its origin is from al-tasjiyah, which is covering, because it conceals with its darkness, as in the verse ﴿And We made the night a garment﴾ [al-Naba': 10].

﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you (ma wadda'aka)﴾ [al-Duha: 3]: this is the answer to the oath, meaning: He has not left you, nor cut you off in the manner of one who bids farewell.

Al-Shihab said in (al-Inayah): "So the tawdi' (farewell) is a metaphor, a continuative metaphor (isti'arah tab'iyyah), for leaving here, and in it there is a subtlety and magnification that is not hidden; for farewell only occurs between loved ones and those whose separation is grievous, as al-Mutanabbi said:

A remnant of a soul bade farewell the day they bade farewell, so I did not know which of the two departing ones to escort."

And he said in (Sharh al-Shifa'): "Wada' has two meanings in the language: leaving, and escorting the traveller. If it is interpreted here in the second sense by way of metaphor, there is in it an allusion that Allah has not left him at all, for He is with him wherever he is. Leaving would only be conceived on his side, and it is apparent. Along with its indication in this meaning of returning, for farewell is only for one who is loved and whose return is hoped for, and al-Urjani alluded to this in his saying:(p-6182)

When you see farewell, be patient, and let not distance trouble you;
and await the return soon, for the heart of farewell is that they return."

So His saying ﴿nor has He detested you﴾ [al-Duha: 3] confirms it. (He said): "I have not seen anyone mention this, despite its great subtlety, and they all interpreted it in the first sense." Since they saw that the form of the verb conveys increase in meaning and intensification, which entails complete severance, they said: the intensification is in the negation, not in the negated thing; so He left him for a judgment upon him, not because of harm from abandoning him, or for negating the condition and the conditioned. It was read: ﴿ma wadda'aka﴾ [al-Duha: 3] with lightened pronunciation (takhfif). And it occurs in a hadith: "The most evil of people is the one whom people leave out of fear of his obscenity." And it occurs in poetry, as in his saying:

"So what they sent forward for their own souls was greater in benefit than what they left behind."

For this reason, he said in (al-Misbah) concerning this: "Know that their saying in the science of morphology that the past tense of yada'u and yadharu is dead (amatu) is an error, and making it a metaphor from wadi'ah (deposit) is far-fetched." End.

Likewise he said in (al-Mustawfi): "All of it occurs in the speech of the Arabs, and the statements of the grammarians regarding it carry no weight; and when the river of Allah comes, the river of Ma'qil is nullified, even if it is rare." End.

And His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿nor has He detested you (qala)﴾ [al-Duha: 3]: that is, nor has He hated you. And al-qali is the one who hates. That is, He did not abandon you out of hatred.

Al-Shihab said: The omission of the object of "qala" is for brevity, since it is known, and so that it follows the pattern of the rhyme-endings (fawasil) after it, or lest He address him with what indicates hatred.

A note (tanbih):

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Abbas that "when the Qur'an was being revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ), Jibril was late to him for some days" (p-6183) so he was reproached for that; the polytheists said: "His Lord has forsaken him and detested him," so Allah revealed this verse. In another narration, the one who said that was the wife of Abu Lahab; in another, that it was Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her. There is no contradiction, given the possibility that it was uttered by all of them, except that the statement of the polytheists and the statement of Khadijah, if authentic, were an expression of grief and sorrow. In the narration of Isma'il, the mawla of the family of al-Zubayr, he said: "Revelation paused until it weighed heavily upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and saddened him. He said: 'I feared that my companion had detested me,' and then Jibril came with the surah 'By the morning brightness.'"

﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the present life﴾ [al-Duha: 4]: Ibn Jarir said: that is, and the abode of the Hereafter and what Allah has prepared for you therein is better for you than the worldly abode and what is in it. He says: so do not grieve over what has escaped you of it, for what is yours with Allah is better for you than it. Al-Qadi said: or: the end of your affair is better than its beginning, for he (ﷺ) continually ascends in elevation and perfection.

﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [al-Duha: 5]: that is, He will give you of the abundance of His blessings in the afterlife until you are satisfied. This is a generous and comprehensive promise, encompassing what Allah the Exalted gave him in this world of perfection of soul, knowledge of the first and the last, the manifestation of the matter and the elevation of the religion, through the conquests that occurred in his time (upon him be prayer and peace), and in the days of his rightly-guided successors and other Muslim rulers, and the spread of his call to the east and west of the earth, and what He stored up for him of honours that no one knows but Allah the Exalted. In sum, this verse comprises the aspects of honour, the kinds of happiness, and the scattered bounties of both abodes, in that He stated it in general terms and left it to His good pleasure, and this is the utmost of kindness and honour.

A note (tanbih):

In (al-Mawahib al-Ladunniyyah) he said: As for what the ignorant are deceived by, that he will not be satisfied with a single one of his community in the Fire, or that he will not be pleased for anyone of his community to enter the Fire, it is from the deception of Satan toward them and his playing with them; for he (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him) is pleased with what his Lord is pleased with, blessed and exalted is He, and He, glorified and exalted, enters into the Fire whoever deserves it from among the disbelievers and the disobedient. The Hashwiyyah have been zealous in strengthening such fabricated reports, deceiving the ignorant and adorning the paths of misguidance. There is no power and no strength except through Allah. And His saying, Exalted is He:

The discussion concerning His words, Exalted is He:

[6–11] ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?﴾ ﴿And find you lost and guide you?﴾ [Ad-Duha: 7] ﴿And find you poor and make you rich?﴾ [Ad-Duha: 8] ﴿As for the orphan, do not oppress him.﴾ [Ad-Duha: 9] ﴿And as for the petitioner, do not repel him.﴾ [Ad-Duha: 10] ﴿And as for the favour of your Lord, proclaim it.﴾ [Ad-Duha: 11]

﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?﴾ Abu al-Su'ud said: This is an enumeration of the great kinds of blessing He bestowed upon him from the beginning of his affair up to that time, so that he may take the present and existing as evidence for the awaited and promised, and thus his heart may be reassured and his breast expanded. The hamza (interrogative particle) here is for emphasising the negation and affirming the negated in the most eloquent manner, as if it were said: "He has indeed found you," etc. And wujud (finding) here means knowledge ('ilm).

It is narrated that "his father died while he was in the womb, six months after conception, and his mother died when he was eight years old, so his paternal uncle Abu Talib took charge of him, and Allah inclined him towards him, and he raised him well." This is the "giving of refuge." ﴿And find you lost and guide you?﴾ [Ad-Duha: 7] That is: unaware of what He had revealed to you of guidance and the Criterion, so He guided you to it and made you a leader for others, as in the verse: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾ [Ash-Shura: 52].

Al-Shihab said: Here "dalal" (going astray) is a metaphor drawn from the expression "he strayed on his path," when one takes a road that does not lead to its destination, because of the absence of what would lead him to beneficial knowledge through the way of acquisition.

﴿And find you poor and make you rich?﴾ [Ad-Duha: 8] That is: poor, ﴿and make you rich﴾ [Ad-Duha: 8], that is: He enriched you with the wealth of Khadijah, which she gave to you, or with what you gained from the profit of trade.

﴿As for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾ [Ad-Duha: 9] — do not overpower him regarding his wealth so that you take away his right, seeking his goodwill.

﴿And as for the petitioner, do not repel him﴾ [Ad-Duha: 10] Ibn Jarir said: That is: as for whoever asks you out of need, do not rebuff him, but give him food and fulfil his need, because the petitioner has a right, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And those in whose wealth there is a known right﴾ [Al-Ma'arij: 24] ﴿for the petitioner and the deprived﴾ [Al-Ma'arij: 25].

Al-Hasan — as reported by al-Razi — held that by "the petitioner" is meant one who asks for knowledge, so that it corresponds to His words: ﴿And find you lost and guide you?﴾ [Ad-Duha: 7]. Likewise Ibn Kathir said: That is, just as you were lost and Allah guided you, so do not repel the one who asks about knowledge seeking guidance. Al-Imam (al-Razi) said: This meaning is supported by what was reported concerning the people who used to ask him, peace be upon him, to explain what was unclear to them: among them were the People of the Book who disputed, and among them were the rough Bedouins, and among them were those who asked about what prophets are not asked about. So it is no wonder that Allah commands him to be gentle with them and forbids him to repel them, just as He rebuked him for turning away from the blind petitioner in Surah Abasa. End of quotation.

﴿And as for the favour of your Lord, proclaim it﴾ [Ad-Duha: 11] That is: by thanking Him for it and displaying its effects, so that others desire what is with Him of it, and are eager that the needy depart from it satisfied. This is the secret of the command to speak of it. The verse also alerts to a great etiquette, which is to undertake to speak of the blessing and make it known, out of eagerness for generosity and bounty and adopting the character of magnanimity, and fleeing from the vile trait of miserliness, whose leader is concealing the blessing, feigning poverty and complaining.

Al-Imam said: It is the habit of misers to conceal their wealth, so that the argument may stand for them in withholding their hands from giving; so you find them only complaining of scarcity. As for the generous, they continually display through giving what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty, and they openly praise Him for what He has poured out upon them of His provision. Therefore it is correct that speaking of the blessing be made a metaphor for giving, feeding the poor and helping the needy. This is what is meant by His words: ﴿And as for the favour of your Lord, proclaim it﴾ [Ad-Duha: 11], that is: since you have come to know from your own experience what the poor man undergoes, then be lavish in giving to the poor. The aim is not merely the mention of wealth, for this is boasting which the Prophet ﷺ was far above; nor is it known from him, in carrying out this command, that he mentioned what he had of money and goods; rather what is known of him is that "he would spend what he had and spend the night hungry." It may be said that by the blessing is meant prophethood, but the context of the verses indicates that this verse corresponds to His words: ﴿And find you poor﴾ [Ad-Duha: 8], so the blessing means wealth; and if it meant prophethood, it would correspond to His words: ﴿And find you lost﴾ [Ad-Duha: 7], and you have already known the truth regarding that. And Allah knows best.
